published_statement: Classification (Martin-Moruno & Visser 2102.13551 sec 2.2, restating Hawking-Ellis [14]): 'The Hawking-Ellis (Segre-Plebanski) classification of stress-energy tensors is composed of four different types. Each type represents a different eigenvector structure. Those are: type I, which has 1 timelike and 3 spacelike eigenvectors; type II, with 1 double null eigenvector and 2 spacelike eigenvectors; type III, which has 1 triple null eigenvector and 1 spacelike eigenvector; and type IV, which has no causal eigenvector.' Canonical form eq (2.3): T^ab = [[rho,f1,f2,0],[f1,p1,sigma,0],[f2,sigma,p2,0],[0,0,0,p3]] with 'f1 != 0, f2 = sigma = 0, and p1 = -rho for type IV'. Sec 2.2.4: 'There are 2 real spacelike and 2 complex eigenvectors, therefore, no causal (timelike or null) eigenvectors ... there is no physical timelike observer who measures no fluxes. There are no known classical matter fields that lead to a type IV stress-energy tensor.' 1702.05915 sec 2.1: 'Classically, type IV does not seem to occur in nature ... The only way that any of the standard energy conditions can be satisfied for a type IV stress-energy tensor is if f = 0, in which case it reduces to type I.' Maeda-Harada 2205.12993: 'the type IV energy-momentum tensor violates all the standard energy conditions' (after eq 2.16). APPLICATION (Le 2602.18023v6, Table 2, v_s = 0.5, R_b = 1, sigma = 8, wall f in [0.1, 0.9], proper-volume weighted): 'Alcubierre 1.3 [% Type I] 98.7 [% Type IV]'; sec 3.1: 'The Alcubierre, Natario, and Van den Broeck walls are Type-IV dominated (81-99% at v_s = 0.5) ... an established Type-IV tensor has no timelike eigenvector and violates all four energy conditions'; abstract: 'These numerical type labels and sampled fractions are distinct from the interval bounds'; sec 2: 'Type IV: One complex-conjugate eigenvalue pair and two real eigenvalues, with no causal eigenvector. Numerical labels depend on the classification tolerances (Section 1.2).' Le 2606.22531v3 item (e): 'the Alcubierre/Natario class is excluded, its wall stress being observer-robustly Hawking-Ellis Type IV (a complex eigenvalue pair, no rest frame [19])'.
published_hypotheses: H1 four-dimensional Lorentzian spacetime, real symmetric T_ab, classification of the Lorentz-invariant eigenvalue problem det(T^a_b - lambda delta^a_b) = 0 by the causal character of eigenvectors (1702.05915 eq 2.8; 2102.13551 sec 2.2)
H2 the classification is pointwise: a type is a property of T at an event, and it may change between regions (2505.02210 Fig. 9; Le 2602.18023 Table 2 reports fractions, not a global type)

H3 the 'no known' statement is scoped to CLASSICAL matter fields (2102.13551 sec 2.2.4; 1702.05915 'Classically, type IV does not seem to occur in nature'); for quantum test fields Type IV occurs (2102.13551 abstract: Unruh vacuum, massless scalar, Schwarzschild; 1607.05280 p.17)
H4 Type IV violates the NEC and hence every standard pointwise energy condition (1702.05915 sec 2.1; 2205.12993 after eq 2.16; Le 2602.18023 sec 2 'violates the NEC')

H5 (application) Alcubierre 1994 metric with bubble centre x_s(t) moving at v_s, tanh profile, R_b = 1, sigma = 8, v_s = 0.5, evaluated on a constant-t slice with its time dependence (Le 2602.18023 eq (1) with r_s = [(x - x_s(t))^2 + y^2 + z^2]^(1/2))
H6 (application) the Alcubierre Type IV label is NUMERICAL, tolerance-dependent and a sampled fraction (98.7 %), distinct from Le's interval certificates (2602.18023 abstract and sec 2)
hypothesis_drift: METRIC SUBSTITUTED (drops H5), typefour.py:108-110 and :138 ('The configuration is static in these coordinates, so d_t g = 0'): typefour.py differentiates g with shift v_s f(sqrt(x^2+y^2+z^2)) and the bubble centre FIXED at the origin. Alcubierre's metric has r_s = |x - v_s t| (time-dependent); its stationary (comoving) chart has shift -v_s(1 - f), not v_s f. These are different spacetimes: at 6 of the 7 WALL_POINTS the Ricci scalar differs (e.g. (0.90,0.30): R = +8.290 Alcubierre vs -1.396 for typefour's metric; rederive C2d), and typefour.py's printed ||T|| and |Im|/||T|| (typefour.py:47-53) reproduce the substituted metric to 6 figures, not Alcubierre's (Alcubierre: 0.278 / 0.2815 at (0.90,0.30) against the printed 0.15909 / 0.6425). The only agreeing row is (1.00,0.00). typefour.py:23 'The Alcubierre stress-energy is computed here from scratch' is therefore a discrepancy. The Type IV LABEL survives the correction at all 7 points (rederive C2a).

VALIDATION BLIND TO THE SUBSTITUTION, typefour.py:35-38 (BBV Eq 3.48 check): the Eulerian energy density depends only on the extrinsic curvature of the slice, which the two metrics share at t = 0; rederive C3 gives |T^00_lab - T^00_static| <= 3.5e-32 at every wall point. The check is valid for what it checks and cannot detect the missing d_t terms, which enter only the spatial stresses.

SCOPE WIDENED (drops H3), typefour.py:15-16 and :20 ('every substance anyone has ever handled is Type I -- ordinary matter, fields, and the Casimir vacuum included'; 'NOTHING KNOWN IS TYPE IV') and anec.py:71 ('the matter has no rest frame (Type IV)' carried as 'about KIND'): the sources scope the absence to CLASSICAL matter. 2102.13551 abstract: 'For test fields it is not too difficult to get a type IV stress-energy via quantum vacuum polarization effects (For example, consider the Unruh quantum vacuum state for a massless scalar field in the Schwarzschild background.)'; 1607.05280 p.17: conformal scalar in the Unruh state 'Type IV everywhere outside the horizon'. The tree's own paper/CLAIMS.md headline H4 ('Type IV matter is not hypothetical: it sources a metric, and the solution is an evaporating black hole') already contradicts typefour.py:20. Also typefour.py:15 lists 'fields' as Type I while typefour.py:16-17 places radiation in Type II; the Maxwell null field is Type II (internal inconsistency, minor).

INDEPENDENCE FROM ENERGY CONDITIONS OVERSTATED (drops H4), typefour.py:57-63 ('Type IV is a statement about the tensor's eigenvectors. You can make the contractions as small as you like and the eigenvalues stay complex. The two questions are orthogonal') and typefour.py:9 'UNTOUCHED BY EVERY WORD OF THAT': the published result is that Type IV IMPLIES violation of the NEC and so of every standard pointwise condition (1702.05915 sec 2.1; 2205.12993; Le 2602.18023 sec 2). Machine-checked here (rederive C1b, z3 unsat): no Type-IV boost block satisfies T(k,k) >= 0 on both radial null vectors. The type is scale-invariant (true: shrinking T does not change it), but Type IV is a SUBSET of NEC violation, not orthogonal to it. It is orthogonal only to AVERAGED conditions and magnitude bounds, which is what typefour's argument actually needs.

POINTWISE PROPERTY GLOBALISED (drops H2), typefour.py:18 ('no observer, anywhere, for whom it has a rest frame') and anec.py:71 ('the matter has no rest frame'): Type IV is pointwise; Le's Table 2 puts 1.3 % of the Alcubierre wall at Type I; rederive C5 measures 98.84 % Type IV (1.16 % not) on the true metric at the same parameters. 'Type-IV dominated', not 'everywhere'.

NUMERICAL LABEL NOT MARKED AS SUCH (drops H6), typefour.py:48-56 and paper/CLAIMS.md:104 ('PROVEN (numerically, doubly validated)'): Le states his Alcubierre labels are numerical and tolerance-dependent, distinct from his interval certificates. The tree's own 7-point labels are also numerical (Durand-Kerner roots, threshold 1e-3 on |Im|/||T||). Rederive C2 re-derives them from an exact symbolic Einstein tensor at 30 digits, so at these 7 points the label is not a tolerance artefact (min |Im|/||T|| = 0.049 on the true metric), but the evidence is still a finite sample, not a certificate.

CITATION DISCREPANCY, typefour.py:55 ('the classification Le's Table 1 states for the Alcubierre class') and paper/CLAIMS.md:106: in the versions read, Table 1 of Le 2606.22531v3 (the Le paper typefour.py:17 cites for the photon-rocket exterior) has columns Bulk nec / Obs.-robust dec / Accel. / Mechanism / Energy / FTL and NO Hawking-Ellis type column; the Alcubierre Type IV classification is in Le 2602.18023v6 TABLE 2 (98.7 %) and in 2606.22531v3 item (e) as a citation to [19]. Earlier versions (2602.18023 v1-v5) were not read and may have numbered it Table 1. A reference discrepancy, not a refutation.

D-INDEPENDENCE ASSERTED, TESTED AT ONE POINT, anec.py:70 and :210 (chk('Type IV is D-independent and about kind', typefour.is_type_iv((0.9, 0.3, 0.0)), True)): the check runs one point at one wall steepness (sigma = 8) and cannot test independence of D. Measured here on the true metric (rederive C5): wall Type-IV fraction 0.9908 (sigma=4), 0.9884 (8), 0.9769 (16), 0.9562 (32) -- Type IV dominates at every thickness tested over a factor 8 in D, so the word survives as 'persists', but the fraction is not D-invariant, and a factor-8 scan is not a proof for all D.

rederivation.outcome: ALL CHECKS OK (output banked at rederive/hawking-ellis-type-iv-classification.out and .out.json). C1 (sympy + z3): the Hawking-Ellis boost block has discriminant (rho+p)^2 - 4f^2; when negative, z3 returns unsat for any real eigenvalue (no causal eigenvector) and unsat for NEC holding on both radial null vectors -- Type IV implies NEC violation, as published. C2 (exact symbolic Einstein tensor, 30-digit mpmath eigenvalues): the TRUE Alcubierre metric (x_s = v t, t = 0) is Type IV at all 7 typefour.py wall points, min |Im|/||T|| = 0.049; the comoving chart reproduces its Ricci scalar exactly; typefour.py's printed numbers reproduce, to 6 figures, a DIFFERENT metric (bubble fixed at origin, shift v f), whose Ricci scalar differs from Alcubierre's at 6 of 7 points. C3: the BBV Eulerian-density validation agrees between the two metrics to 3.5e-32, so it could not have caught the substitution. C4: the comoving Killing vector is not hypersurface-orthogonal off-axis ((xi ^ dxi)_txy = -y f'(r)((1-f)^2+4)/(8r) != 0), so Maeda/MMV's 'static => Type I' theorem does not apply -- consistent; on the axis all 80 samples with ||T|| > 1e-6 are Type IV. C5: proper-volume-weighted wall Type-IV fraction on the true metric = 0.9884 at sigma = 8 (Le Table 2: 0.987 -- reproduced), and 0.9908 / 0.9769 / 0.9562 at sigma = 4 / 16 / 32.

lacked_data: Hawking & Ellis (1973) stated a taxonomy: it is definitional and uses no data, and nothing learned since changes a definition -- the classification itself re-derives here (C1). What they and the 1970s catalogue lacked is SEMICLASSICAL data: renormalized stress tensors of quantum fields on black-hole backgrounds. When that came (Roman 1986 per MMV; MMV 2017; Abdolrahimi-Page-Tzounis 2019), Type IV turned out to occur for quantum test fields (Unruh vacuum). So M's hypothesis holds for the catalogue claim, and it cuts AGAINST the tree's sentence, not against the outside result: 'nothing known is Type IV' is out of date, while the published 'no known CLASSICAL field' still stands. Then MMV 2021 supplied data the 2017 picture lacked, namely back-reaction, and it narrows the other way: in static exteriors, on Killing horizons and on stationary axes Type IV is excluded. For the application, the tree lacked Le's full-wall measurement and a metric carrying the bubble's motion. With both supplied here, the conclusion 'the Alcubierre wall at v_s = 0.5 is Type-IV dominated' does not move: 98.84 % on the true metric against Le's 98.7 %, and 7/7 at the sampled points. What moves is typefour.py's printed numbers (they belong to a different metric), 'anywhere' (1.2 % of the wall is not Type IV), and 'orthogonal to the energy conditions' (Type IV implies NEC violation). Evidence the other way: Le reports the Type IV fraction falling with speed (wall Type I rising to 24.9 % at v_s = 2.5) and Rodal's irrotational profile being Type I everywhere, so Type IV belongs to the curl-bearing Alcubierre/Natario class at these speeds. It is not a property of warp metrics in general, and the tree's 'Alcubierre class' scoping (typefour.py:73-76) is correct on that point.
grade_evidence: STANDS for the external content. The Hawking-Ellis taxonomy (Type IV = complex eigenvalue pair, no causal eigenvector, violates every standard energy condition) re-derives exactly (C1, sympy + z3). The Alcubierre application re-derives on the TRUE metric: 7/7 wall points Type IV (C2) and a wall fraction of 98.84 % against Le's 98.7 % at identical parameters (C5). NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class than the sources support, each point with its site. (1) typefour.py:20, :15 'NOTHING KNOWN IS TYPE IV' drops the published 'classical' qualifier; the Unruh-state quantum vacuum is Type IV (2102.13551 abstract; 1607.05280 p.17), and the tree's own paper/CLAIMS.md H4 says so. (2) typefour.py:57-63 'orthogonal' to the energy conditions contradicts the published implication Type IV => NEC violated (z3 unsat, C1b); the orthogonality holds only for averaged and magnitude conditions. (3) typefour.py:18 and anec.py:71 globalise a pointwise type ('no observer, anywhere'), while about 1.2-1.3 % of the wall is not Type IV. (4) anec.py:70/:210 'D-independent' is checked at one point and one sigma; measured here over sigma 4-32, Type IV persists (99.1 % -> 95.6 %) but the fraction is not invariant. Recorded as DISCREPANCIES, not refutations, and nothing is repaired: typefour.py:108-110/:138 differentiates a static metric that is not Alcubierre's (Ricci scalar differs at 6/7 points; the printed ||T|| and ratios belong to it; the BBV validation is blind to it, C3), yet the Type IV label survives the correction at every point; and 'Le's Table 1' (typefour.py:55) is Table 2 of 2602.18023v6 in the versions read. Nothing here is WRONG. The label anec.py actually checks, typefour.is_type_iv((0.9,0.3,0)), is true on the correct metric as well (|Im|/||T|| = 0.2815).
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree scopes its sentences to 'no known classical matter', 'Type-IV dominated wall', and 'orthogonal to averaged/magnitude conditions (Type IV itself implies pointwise NEC violation)', and computes the moving-bubble metric. Nothing here would take the classification itself to WRONG. The Alcubierre label would be WRONG only if an interval-certified evaluation of the true metric found the wall predominantly Type I at v_s = 0.5, sigma = 8, which neither Le's numerics nor the 30-digit symbolic evaluation here supports. Reading 2102.13551 sec 3.5 (p.17) would settle whether the on-axis Type IV found here sits outside MMV's hypotheses (expected) or is a discrepancy with their theorem. A discover_papers search, blocked by quota here, could turn up later work that narrows further. Reading 2602.18023 v1-v5 would settle whether 'Table 1' was once correct.
